description: Hi, We are team OrbitX Alfa, working on the 'Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions' challenge. We have skills in coding and software development, and we are looking for teammates interested in UI/UX design, health data analysis, and presentation. Let's build an awesome health tracking solution together.
summary:
AstroGuard is a project we developed to explore how astronauts' health can be monitored during space missions. Space is a challenging environment, and astronauts may face different health problems during long missions. Our aim was to bring some important health and cabin environment information together in one platform.

The project includes a 3D human body, vital signs monitoring, webcam-based eye and face tracking, and a cabin environment monitoring system. It can display possible warning conditions using red, yellow, and green indicators. It also includes graphs and mission simulations to help users understand how health and environmental conditions may change over time. The cabin monitoring section covers CO2, oxygen, pressure, temperature, and humidity.

We developed AstroGuard using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, along with Three.js and MediaPipe. We wanted to make health information easier to understand through visual features instead of showing only numbers.

This project addresses the challenge by demonstrating how different health indicators and environmental conditions can be observed in one place. I hope this idea can support learning and inspire further work on astronaut health monitoring. AstroGuard is a prototype and is not yet tested or certified for real medical use.
details:
Our project is called AstroGuard. It is a health monitoring system prototype made for astronauts during space missions.

The main aim of this project is to show how an astronaut's health and cabin environment can be monitored in one place. It includes a 3D human body, vital signs monitoring, webcam-based eye and face tracking, and a cabin environment section. It can show different health indicators and use red, yellow, and green colors to highlight possible warning conditions. It also monitors cabin factors like CO2, oxygen, pressure, temperature, and humidity. There are also graphs and mission simulations to help understand how these conditions may change over time.

This project can help people understand the health problems astronauts may face during long space missions. It brings different information together, so it is easier to observe and understand possible risks.

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the project. We also used Three.js for the 3D human body and MediaPipe Face Mesh and Camera Utils for webcam-based face and eye tracking. The project runs in a web browser.

The interesting part is not only the numbers but a 3D body which shows where a possible health warning is related. We wanted to make the system more visual and easier to understand.

While making this project, we considered the challenges astronauts may face during long missions, such as changes in cabin conditions, limited space, and health risks. We also referred to NASA's Human Research Program resources and other NASA documents while preparing the hazard information.

AstroGuard is currently a student prototype for learning and demonstration. It does not use live NASA spacecraft data and is not a medically certified system.
